'''George Bernard Kauffman''' (September 4, 1930 &ndash; May 2, 2020) was an American chemist.

==Life==
Kauffman was born in Philadelphia, the son of Laura (Fisher) and Joseph Philip Kauffman.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZZxmAAAAMAAJ&q=Philip+Joseph+and+Laura+(Fisher)+Kauffman|title = Who's who in the West|year = 2004| publisher=Marquis-Who's Who. |isbn = 9780837909356}}</ref> He received his bachelor's degree from the [[University of Pennsylvania]], and Ph.D. from the [[University of Florida]]. Kauffman was a professor of chemistry at [[California State University, Fresno]]. He wrote 17 books and over 2,000 articles.

In 1978, George B. Kauffman received the [[Dexter Award for Outstanding Achievement in the History of Chemistry]] from the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="ACSDexter2">{{cite web|url=http://www.scs.illinois.edu/~mainzv/HIST/awards/dexter.php|title=Dexter Award for Outstanding Achievement in the History of Chemistry|website=Division of the History of Chemistry|publisher=American Chemical Society|access-date=30 April 2015}}</ref> He was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.scs.uiuc.edu/~mainzv/HIST/awards/Dexter%20Papers/KauffmanDexterBioJJB.pdf
| title = George B. Kauffman (1930–
| publisher = California State University
| access-date = 2007-08-15
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100612200018/http://www.scs.uiuc.edu/~mainzv/HIST/awards/Dexter%20Papers/KauffmanDexterBioJJB.pdf
| archive-date = 2010-06-12
| url-status = dead
}}</ref>

Kauffman wrote a series of articles with [[Foil A. Miller]] about [[chemistry on stamps]].<ref name=Miller_Kauffman1>{{cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=Foil A.|last2=Kauffman|first2=George B.|title=Alfred Nobel and Philately: The Man, His Work, and His Prizes|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|date=October 1988|volume=65|issue=10|pages=843–846|doi=10.1021/ed065p843|bibcode=1988JChEd..65..843M }}</ref><ref name=Miller_Kauffman2>{{cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=Foil A.|last2=Kauffman|first2=George B.|title=Nobel Laureates in Chemistry - A Philatelic Survey. Part I. 1901-1910|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|date=June 1990|volume=67|issue=6|pages=451–456|doi=10.1021/ed067p451|bibcode=1990JChEd..67..451K }}</ref><ref name=Miller_Kauffman3>{{cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=Foil A.|last2=Kauffman|first2=George B.|title=Nobel Laureates in Chemistry - A Philatelic Survey. Part II. 1911-1934|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|date=July 1990|volume=67|issue=7|pages=569–574|doi=10.1021/ed067p569|bibcode=1990JChEd..67..569K }}</ref><ref name=Miller_Kauffman4>{{cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=Foil A.|last2=Kauffman|first2=George B.|title=Nobel Laureates in Chemistry - A Philatelic Survey. Part III. 1935-1988|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|date=September 1990|volume=67|issue=9|pages=774–781|doi=10.1021/ed067p774|bibcode=1990JChEd..67..774K }}</ref>

Kauffman died on May 2, 2020, at his home in [[Fresno, California]] at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite web|title=George Bernard Kauffman, Obituary|periodical=|publisher=Lisle Funeral Home|url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/obituaries/fresno-ca/george-kauffman-9168328|url-status=|format=|access-date=|archive-url=|archive-date=|last=|date=|year=|language=en|pages=|quote=}}</ref>
